name: Thumbs Down
baseMeaning: A hand with thumb pointing down, indicating disapproval.
tldr: Disapproval, dislike, or rejection. Direct negative reaction without going nuclear.

platformNotes.note: Reacts to bad takes, dropped shows, and brand apologies where a thumbs-down reads as direct disapproval without dragging the post into quote-tweet territory.
Rarer than 👍 because the platform skews positive, but it surfaces in story polls, group-chat reactions to bad news, and DM replies to plans the sender wants to veto.
Anchors review-style content ('rating every flavor 👎') and ironic 'I hate this but I love it' videos where the thumbs-down reads as banter rather than real criticism.
Acts as the polite 'I disagree' reaction to a proposal in a team channel, especially when paired with a sentence that explains the concern rather than relying on the emoji alone.

generationalNotes.note: Uses 👎 as a sharp disagreement signal in DMs and group chats; pairs it with 😂 or 💀 to soften the read into banter, or with a sentence to land the disapproval as a clear take.
Reaches for 👎 as a clean 'no' reaction - uses it on dropped shows, bad client work, and travel-rant tweets where the thumbs-down reads as direct but not aggressive.
Reads 👎 as a literal dislike and uses it on restaurant reviews, customer-service complaints, and family-chat vetoes without the ironic layer younger users apply.
Treats 👎 as the unambiguous 'no' - uses it on political posts, recipe ratings, and any context where they want to register clear disapproval without writing a longer reply.

warnings.title: Can read as confrontational in work channels
warnings.description: Sending 👎 as the sole reaction to a coworker's proposal reads as harsh. Pair it with a sentence that explains the concern, or use a softer emoji and a private DM for serious pushback.

warnings.title: Avoid in moments of vulnerability
warnings.description: A 👎 reply to a friend who shared a recipe, a photo, or a vulnerable disclosure reads as cruel. Use a sentence, a different reaction, or silence rather than a literal thumbs-down on something personal.

seoTitle: 👎 Thumbs Down Emoji Meaning - What Does 👎 Really Mean?
seoDescription: Learn what the Thumbs Down emoji 👎 really means in modern texting. Disapproval, rejection, and how to use it without sounding harsh.

longForm.overview:
👎 is the universal negative reaction emoji - the digital shorthand for 'no,' 'dislike,' or 'this is not it.' The thumbs-down gesture has a long cultural history (it dates back to gladiatorial Rome and was the standard 'reject' signal in 20th-century boardrooms) which is why the emoji translates instantly across audiences. There is no specialized slang to decode, no platform where it reads as unfamiliar, and no generational group that misreads it. A 👎 means 'I do not like this' in any chat from any sender.

What is interesting about 👎 in 2026 is how lightly it lands compared to the gesture it represents. In person, a thumbs-down can feel sharp - the universal sign of rejection, a failed job interview, a contestant who got voted off. As an emoji it sits closer to a shrug: it lets a sender register disapproval without writing out a paragraph, which is why it is so common in reaction threads, group chats, and review replies where the user wants to acknowledge a take without escalating into a debate.

The emoji also carries a strong ironic layer that did not exist in its physical form. Younger users will send 👎 on a tweet that they actually enjoyed as part of a 'I hate that I love this' bit, or pair it with 😂 to soften the read into banter. That ironic softening is what makes 👎 travel safely across work DMs, family group chats, and friend threads without sounding aggressive - context and pairing usually telegraph the intent faster than the icon itself.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👎 shows up as a reaction to a dropped show ('the finale 👎'), a one-line review of a restaurant ('overpriced and cold 👎'), and a vote against a plan ('canceling on me again? 👎'). It pairs naturally with sentences that explain the reaction - 'the finale was rushed 👎,' 'this place was not worth it 👎' - and with other emojis that soften or sharpen the read.

In work contexts 👎 acts as the polite 'I disagree' reaction to a proposal in a team channel. A 'timeline is too aggressive 👎' Slack message reads as direct disagreement without forcing the sender into a multi-paragraph rebuttal. Pairing the thumbs-down with a sentence that explains the concern - 'shipping that fast locks us out of QA' - tends to land better than the emoji alone.

The emoji also shows up in rating contexts. A 'rating every flavor in the bag 👎👎👎' TikTok video uses the thumbs-down as the badge for the worst entries, where the repetition reads as comedy. In group chats 👎 punctuates vetoes ('pizza again? 👎'), vetoed plans ('Saturday is rough for me 👎'), and reaction threads ('oh no 👎') where the senders want to acknowledge a bad update without making it the whole conversation.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 👎 in work channels as the sole reaction to a coworker's proposal or work. A lone thumbs-down on someone's idea reads as harsh and is the kind of small moment that becomes a resentment. Pair it with a sentence that explains the concern, or send your pushback in a private DM rather than the channel.

Skip 👎 in moments of vulnerability. A thumbs-down reply to a friend who shared a recipe, a poem, a vulnerable disclosure, or a creative project reads as cruel - the icon is too direct for a moment that needed warmth. Use a sentence, a different reaction, or silence rather than a literal thumbs-down on something personal.

Avoid 👎 in early dating or with people you do not know well. The disapproval cue can land sharper than the sender intends, especially in cross-cultural conversations where the thumbs-down gesture carries different weight. When in doubt, write a sentence that explains the reaction instead of relying on the icon.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 👎 as a reaction to a plan or proposal, mirror with a sentence that responds to the concern ('fair, let me think about timing') rather than sending a fourth thumbs-down in a row. If you want to escalate the disagreement, follow with a clearer argument - 'here is why I think this works' - rather than stacking the emoji.

When 👎 lands as part of a rating or review ('that place was a 👎'), mirror with your own take or send 👍 if you disagree. When it arrives in a banter thread ('healthy eating 👎'), pair with 😂 or 💀 to keep the read playful. And if 👎 shows up as an ironic 'I hate this but I love it' reaction, mirror with another ironic emoji - 👎, 💀, or 🥲 - to match the joke.

faqs.question: What does 👎 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: From a guy, 👎 means 'I do not like this' - same as it does from anyone else. The thumbs-down carries no gendered meaning; it is the universal negative reaction emoji regardless of who sends it.

faqs.question: Is 👎 passive-aggressive?
faqs.answer: It can be. A lone 👎 in response to a friend's suggestion or a coworker's proposal reads as dismissive or passive-aggressive, depending on the relationship. Pairing the emoji with a sentence that explains the concern usually lands better than the icon on its own.

faqs.question: What does 👎 mean from a woman?
faqs.answer: From a woman, 👎 means 'I do not like this' or 'this is not it' - the same as it does from anyone else. The thumbs-down gesture is not gendered; it is the cleanest negative-reaction emoji on the keyboard and reads the same regardless of the sender.

faqs.question: Is 👎 okay at work?
faqs.answer: In Slack and other work channels, 👎 can read as confrontational when used as a sole reaction to a coworker's proposal. Pair it with a sentence that explains the concern, or send your pushback in a private DM. In casual channels and on personal messages the thumbs-down is fine as a clean 'no' reaction.

conversationExamples.message: shipping the launch Friday with no QA cycle 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: Coworker pushing back on a risky timeline. Mirror with a sentence that addresses the concern ('fair, let me re-check the QA buffer') rather than another thumbs-down that escalates the disagreement.

conversationExamples.message: canceling on me for the third time 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: Partner or date registering real frustration about reliability. Mirror with an apology sentence and a plan to make it right; a fourth 👎 would only escalate the tension.
Friend giving a sharp take on a show. Mirror with your own rating, 😂, or a sentence that matches the take; stacking another 👎 on a joke thread turns the joke into a complaint.

conversationExamples.message: rating the new coffee shop: overpriced and tiny 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: Friend sharing a one-line review. Mirror with 👍 if you had a better experience, or a sentence that matches the take ('yeah the line was forever') to validate the read.

conversationExamples.message: dad just sent a thumbs-down to the family group chat photo of dinner 👎
conversationExamples.interpretation: Sibling narrating the parent's blunt reaction. Mirror with 😂 or 💀 to acknowledge the dad's dry humor rather than another 👎 that would read as agreeing with his critique.
